findings.issue: lit_en is the literal of a different sentence (a price question, e.g. りんごはいくら 'how much is an apple'); りんごがほしい? contains no price word at all — it is 'apple-NOM wanted?'. Template residue, teaches the wrong structure.

Garbled literal mirror, apparently residue of the same price template as lit_en: spurious 'que' (there is no interrogative word in the JP) and masculine 'querido' for maçã. Should mirror [maçã-が desejada(-é)?].

'Why not?' drops the entire content of ぜひそうしよう ('by all means, let's do that') and contradicts pt ('Com certeza, vamos fazer assim!') and lit_en; it only works as a loose dialogue reply, so as the sentence's translation it is misleading.
findings.suggested: By all means, let's do that.

findings.issue: Typo in the で token's note, in both languages: the causal connector is written 'のので' instead of 'ので' (en: 'part of the causal connector のので'). A learner could think the pattern carries an extra の.
findings.current: で aqui faz parte do conector causal のので
findings.suggested: で aqui faz parte do conector causal ので

findings.issue: Literal mirror inserts 'in', turning the nominal predicate 気じゃなかった ('wasn't the (usual) mind') into the unrelated English idiom 'wasn't in the mood'; it contradicts lit_pt ('ânimo não-era') and the expl's own literal reading.
findings.current: The mood (subject) wasn't in the mood (past).
